doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

title: 'Peaceful Thinking' and 'Jakuba's Dance'
summary: Rowe sings a Griffin tune; Griffin identifies 'Peaceful Thinking' and explains 'Jakuba's Dance' was written for his young son.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. All right. I’m going to try something out on you and you’ll have to forgive my vocals.
But I want to see if — this is a Dick Griffin song from — if I don’t deliver it very well I’ll give you a hint that I believe it’s about 40 years old. Okay, here we go: [scats].
“Peaceful Thinking” that’s on my first record.
I’m not really hearing the keyboard over Zoom. So was there an inspiration for that?
Yeah that’s my son. And when he was a small kid, like two years old, he would be trying to dance and he would be jumping around and bouncing around and I called it “Jakuba’s Dance.”

Yes. It’s lovely. And I noticed when I was trying to practice just doing the melody, it sounds almost like pentatonic, a little bit without the accompaniment. It sounds like a sound from an Asian country.
